solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Inspired by others, teach self-control

indicators.note: something inspired is breathed in, so the teaching word is taken into the middle of the word for others

parts.note: the rest means the others
to train is to teach

explanation.surface: A lesson in self-discipline picked up by watching how other people behave.
explanation.definitionFit: Restraint is the holding back of one's own impulses, a synonym for self-control.

clue.text: Blue vehicle overturning at end of motorway

indicators.note: in a down answer, overturning flips the vehicle word upside down so it reads backwards

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: the end of motorway is its final letter

parts.note: last letter of motorway

explanation.surface: A blue car flips over at the end of a motorway in a crash.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue in the sense of risqué or smutty matches racy, describing mildly indecent material.

clue.text: Absence of sound, as involving the French

indicators.note: involving means wrapping round, so the word for as takes the French article inside it

parts.note: as in the sense of because or since
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A grammatical remark about how the French language handles quiet, or a gap in a recording.
explanation.definitionFit: Silence is the complete lack of any noise, which is an exact paraphrase.

clue.text: Strange game, mah-jong, to begin with

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a game

indicators.note: to begin with points to the opening letter of mah-jong

parts.note: first letter of mah-jong

explanation.surface: Someone finds mah-jong an odd game at first acquaintance.
explanation.walkthrough: RU (rugby union) is a standard crossword abbreviation for a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum is an old-fashioned British word for odd or peculiar.

clue.text: Line on map, one originally standing on counter

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letters of standing and on

parts.note: first letter of standing
first letter of on
a bar is a counter in a pub

explanation.surface: A single person standing at a counter, perhaps in a pub, described in map terms.
explanation.definitionFit: An isobar is a line on a weather chart joining places of equal atmospheric pressure.

clue.text: Exciting fact about small stream

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word for fact surrounds the stream word

parts.note: a thing can be a fact (one thing is certain)
a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: An enthusiast shares a stirring piece of information about a little brook.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrilling describes something that excites strongly, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Little Christopher's gear

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a pet form of the name Christopher

explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as is, linking the two meanings rather than showing possession.
explanation.definitionFit: Kit is both a short form of the name Christopher and a word for a set of equipment or sports clothing.

clue.text: Grilled dish from kitchen initially upset tiny child

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of kitchen

parts.note: first letter of kitchen

indicators.note: in a down answer upset turns the child word upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: a babe is a tiny child

explanation.surface: A toddler knocks over a plate of food that has come out of the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: A kebab is meat and vegetables on a skewer cooked over a grill.

clue.text: Note from singer picked up by audience

indicators.note: what an audience picks up is what it hears, so the singer word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a tenor is a male singer

explanation.surface: A musical note from a singer that the audience catches.
explanation.walkthrough: A tenner is British slang for a ten-pound banknote; in a non-rhotic British accent it sounds like tenor. 'Note' looks musical but is money.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenner is a ten-pound banknote, so note here means paper money.

clue.text: Small jazz group touring most of old Asian capital

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the jazz group's letters surround the trimmed word

parts.note: a combo is a small jazz band

indicators.note: most of means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as the word OLD

explanation.surface: A jazz band goes on tour around a former Asian capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Colombo is the largest city and commercial capital of Sri Lanka, long its seat of government.

clue.text: Possibly mug popular singer

parts.note: to mug someone is to rob them
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A popular singer might be the target of a mugging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' signals that the definition is an example: a robin is one kind of songbird. 'Singer' looks like a pop star but is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The robin is a songbird, so it is an example of a singer.

clue.text: Impregnable base in USA, all newly set out

indicators.note: set out anew means arranged afresh, so the letters are laid out in a new order

explanation.surface: A military base in America with all its defences freshly arranged is impossible to attack.
explanation.definitionFit: An unassailable position cannot be attacked or captured, the same idea as impregnable.

clue.text: Reconstructed in Burma, extremely secure warship

indicators.note: reconstructed means built again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged
extremely points to the outermost letters of secure

parts.note: first and last letters of secure

explanation.surface: A warship rebuilt in Burma to be extremely safe.
explanation.definitionFit: A submarine is an underwater naval vessel, a kind of warship.

clue.text: Part of speech from bishop backing retired vicar, perhaps

indicators.note: backing means the bishop's letter comes at the back, after the other piece
retired means drawn back, so the clergyman's title is read backwards

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is the title of a vicar among others
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop supports a vicar who has stepped down from his parish.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb is a word class, the grammatical category for action or state words.

clue.text: Greek character involved in radio talks

indicators.note: involved in means contained within, so the letters lie inside the words radio talks

explanation.surface: A Greek figure takes part in discussions on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: Iota is the ninth letter of the Greek alphabet; character here means letter.

clue.text: Doctor drank a pint, finally — from this?

definitions.text: Doctor drank a pint, finally — from this?

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of pint

parts.note: last letter of pint

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are altered

explanation.surface: A physician downs a pint at last, and the clue asks what vessel he drank it from.
explanation.walkthrough: The final T of pint leads, then A, then NKARD, the rearranged DRANK.
explanation.definitionFit: A tankard is a large beer mug, the sort of vessel a pint is drunk from.

clue.text: Afterthought about one's church sign

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the afterthought letters go round the rest

parts.note: PS, postscript, is an afterthought added to a letter
one is I, so one's is I'S
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A postscript added to a letter about someone's church noticeboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Pisces, the fish, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Evaluate a couple of vessels rounding end of cape

indicators.note: rounding means going round, so the two ship abbreviations enclose the letter from cape

parts.note: SS (steamship) is a vessel, so a couple of them is SS SS

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of cape

parts.note: last letter of cape

explanation.surface: Assessing a pair of ships as they sail round the tip of a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: To assess is to judge the worth or quality of something, a synonym of evaluate.

clue.text: Uncompromising senior officer being conveyed outside

indicators.note: outside means the phrase for being conveyed goes round the officer's letters

parts.note: in transit means being carried from place to place
GEN is short for general, a senior officer

explanation.surface: A stubborn high-ranking officer being transported somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: An intransigent person refuses to change their views or reach agreement.

clue.text: Vagrant's cunning raised by political representative

indicators.note: in a down answer raised means lifted up, so the cunning word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: art can mean cunning or craft
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A homeless person's wiliness is brought up by a member of parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's in Vagrant's reads as is.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramp is a homeless wanderer, the same as a vagrant.

clue.text: Endure Paddington, for example

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to put up with
second meaning: Paddington is a famous fictional ...

explanation.walkthrough: Paddington looks like the London station, but it is the bear from Michael Bond's children's books.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to tolerate something and also names the animal Paddington is an instance of.

clue.text: Omnivorous mammal in Channel Islands eating grass

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the islands' letters swallow the grass

parts.note: oat is a cereal grass

explanation.surface: An animal that eats everything is found grazing on one of the Channel Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: The coati is a raccoon-like American animal that eats both plants and small animals.

clue.text: English friend entertaining Irish in Muslim state

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, so the friend word holds the Irish letters

parts.note: a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: An English friend plays host to an Irish guest in a Gulf country.
explanation.definitionFit: An emirate is a territory ruled by an emir, as in the Gulf states.

clue.text: Reportedly looked at small fish

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said aloud, so the answer sounds like the word for looked at

parts.note: eyed means looked at

explanation.surface: Someone is said to have glanced at a little fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The ide is a European freshwater fish of the carp family.

clue.text: Cat briefly comes back to eat or drink

indicators.note: comes back means returns, so the shortened cat word reads backwards
briefly means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: puss is an informal word for a cat

explanation.surface: A cat pops back home for a quick meal or drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts PUSS to PUS, and 'comes back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To sup is to take liquid in sips or to have supper, covering both eating and drinking.

clue.text: Cockney primarily employed as nurse?

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, picking out the opening letter of employed

parts.note: first letter of employed
a tender is one who tends, as a nurse tends patients

explanation.surface: A Cockney working as a nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags tender as a made-up word for one who tends. A Cockney is a working-class Londoner from the East End.
explanation.definitionFit: An East Ender is a resident of London's East End, the traditional home of Cockneys.
